notes:
MAGBL has THREE distinct facilities/tranches, all confirmed by direct sheet inspection of every workbook: (1) main IDCOL tranche (matches EX_DATA['MAGBL'], 175M BDT), (2) a BIFFL co-financier tranche present in every one of the four main-loan workbooks (MAGBL_Loan.xlsx, _Rescheduled_13_12_18, _Restructured, _2nd Restructured_Feb'21) as a parallel "MAGBL_Loan (BIFFL)" / "Repayment Schedule (BIFFL)" tab, numerically distinct from the IDCOL tab (tiny rounding/day-count drift from slightly different disbursement dates: 21-Nov-2016/18-Jan-2017 for BIFFL vs 1-Dec-2016/17-Jan-2017 for IDCOL) — confirmed this is genuinely a separate co-financier ledger, analogous to BPCL's Trust Bank tranche, not a duplicate tab; and (3) the separate 'MAGBL_Loan_Additional' facility (63M BDT, disbursed 24-Jul-2017, Annuity principal), which has no BIFFL split and was not in EX_DATA so its ORIGINAL parameters were extracted directly from MAGBL_Loan_Additional.xlsx as version 0.

IMPORTANT FINDING - the BIFFL tranche is UNCHANGED across all reschedule/restructure events: in every one of the three post-original main-loan workbooks, the "Repayment Schedule (BIFFL)" tab is byte-identical to the original (still 24 installments, matures 15-Jun-2023, no capitalization, no moratorium extension) while only the IDCOL tab was actually modified. I still produced one BIFFL version entry per source file (as instructed, every file must produce at least one version entry) but flagged these as pass-through/unchanged with capitalizedAmount=0 and no rate/tenor change, since the workbook data genuinely shows no BIFFL-side event.

CHRONOLOGY AMBIGUITY (flagged per instructions rather than skipped): both the IDCOL main tranche and the Additional facility have a "Restructured" file (no date suffix) whose numbers are NOT continuous with the "2nd Restructured_Feb'21" file. Concretely: MAGBL_Loan_Rescheduled_13_12_18.xlsx and MAGBL_Loan_Restructured.xlsx both start from the identical opening balance at 13-Dec-2018 (post interest-capitalization jump at 13-Sep-2018) but diverge immediately — Rescheduled_13_12_18 shows a moratorium stall (interest-only Mar'19-Jun'19) while Restructured shows clean immediate amortization with NO capitalization at all and fully amortizes by Sep-2024. Meanwhile MAGBL_Loan_2nd Restructured_Feb'21.xlsx's numbers match Rescheduled_13_12_18's path exactly through Dec-2019 (not Restructured's path), then add a further COVID-era moratorium (Mar'20-Dec'20, interest capitalized quarterly) extending final maturity to Sep-2026. This means "Restructured" is NOT an intermediate step in the chain that "2nd Restructured" built on — it appears to be an alternate/superseded restructuring scenario (possibly a proposal that was not implemented, or a parallel draft) rather than a strict link in the version chain. I have modeled all three IDCOL versions (and their Additional-facility counterparts) as separate version entries with effectiveDate 2018-12-13 for both Rescheduled_13_12_18 and Restructured (since both branch from the same point), and flagged this in case the versioning engine needs to treat "Restructured" as a dead/superseded branch rather than a live link between Rescheduled_13_12_18 and 2nd Restructured. A human should confirm with IDCOL loan-ops which of "Rescheduled_13_12_18" vs "Restructured" was the version actually executed/booked, since 2nd Restructured's continuity implies Rescheduled_13_12_18 (not Restructured) was the operative predecessor.

No rate changes were found anywhere (constant 9% throughout all versions and both facilities). No true waivers (waivedAmount = 0 throughout) — all "reductions" seen are moratorium/capitalization mechanics, not forgiveness. Day-count basis (360) and payment frequency (quarterly) never changed. All override arrays (interest_payment_amounts/opening_balance_amounts/closing_balance_amounts) were used for every non-original version because each involves irregular stub periods (moratorium pauses, interest capitalization jumps) that cannot be cleanly regenerated by the engine's standard amortization formulas from a simple loan_amount+rate+tenor input — this mirrors the override pattern already used for MCML/QPSL/SCBL/SKS/THERMAX in examples.ts. The single-disbursement "rolled-forward balance as of effective date" modeling approach specified in the task was used for every version (disbursements: [[effective_date_serial, opening_balance]]).
